#en:
Some nights I miss the way the whole node would shiver when a heavy freighter cut through the grav window. I knew every tremor in that tower, could tell a HopeTech hauler from a Trident liner just by how the decking hummed. Now my flooring is whatever scrap I could weld together, and the only vibrations are my own making.

They called it an anomaly cluster. Clean phrase for dirty work. I saw the telemetry, the way the same corridor kept getting re-used after every "pilot error," like someone was stress-testing the universe with other people's lives. I flagged it, I argued, I pushed the logs up the chain. What came back down was silence and a recommendation for "rest" and "evaluation."

So I took my own eval and walked.

I picked the fringe because the fringe does not ask questions as long as the beacons line up and the credits clear. Neon, Gagarin, the dustier outposts you only see in LIST brochures they all run on secondhand charts and tired controllers grateful for anyone who can shave a few minutes off a route without putting a ship through a rock. I become "Lira" out here, and "Vector" only when it suits me. Names are just transponders for people.

This place makes sense for what I need. Too far for comfortable UC oversight, close enough to the main lanes that every misfiled waypoint ripples into traffic patterns I can read. I sit in borrowed back rooms, watching their pretty holograms of shipping routes, and underneath I lay my own lattice of corrected paths, quiet warnings, and yes, a few carefully engineered failures. Ghost freighters, dead on paper already, steered somewhere they cannot hurt anyone real. I hijack what they have already written off.

People call me a saboteur because it is easier than admitting the sabotage started on official letterhead.

I keep thinking about this one corridor near Porrima. If I had not bent that route away from the published window, a whole string of civilian hulls would have walked straight into someone else's experiment. A crimson flag, a corporate skunkworks, some MAST subcommittee it does not matter who. If I had not acted, someone worse would have. Someone who did not care who was strapped into the seats when the numbers failed.

I am not stupid. I know what hunts me now. UC SysDef does not black-flag you unless you have made them nervous, and nervous bureaucrats are more dangerous than any Spacer crew. That is why I move my bases, why I leave caches in forgotten kiosks and hollowed-out relays, why I never sleep in the same orbit twice if I can help it. Somewhere out there, a hunter is following the same patterns I did, seeing the same scars in the lanes.

I am afraid, but not of them finding me.

I am afraid they will kill me before I finish rewriting the last of those corridors, before I can prove that the "accidents" were designed, that the insurance spikes and route changes and missing logs all rhyme. Afraid that when I am gone, the traffic will settle back into its old ruts, and nobody will remember why ships keep disappearing in the same quiet stretches of sky.

So I stay out here, on the edge of their maps, listening to the hum of the drives and the whispers in the beacons, waiting for my vectors to intersect with whoever still cares enough to see.
zh:
有些夜里我怀念整个节点在重型货船切过重力窗口时颤抖的样子。我熟悉那座塔里的每一次震颤，单凭甲板的嗡鸣就能分辨霍普科技的货船和三叉戟的班轮。如今我的地板是我能焊到一起的随便什么废料，而唯一的振动是我自己制造的。

他们管它叫"异常集群"。给脏活儿起的好听说法。我看到了遥测，看那条走廊如何在每一次"飞行员失误"后被重复使用，像有人在拿别人的性命对宇宙做压力测试。我标记了它、我争辩了、我把日志往上推。回到我手里的是沉默，以及一句关于"休息"和"评估"的建议。

于是我做了自己的评估，然后走了。

我选了外缘，因为只要你信标库对得上、信用币到账，外缘就不问问题。霓虹城、加加林、那些只在独立盟宣传册里见得到的尘土前哨——它们全靠二手星图和疲惫的管制员运转，那些人只要有人能替他们把航线削掉几分钟又不让飞船撞上岩石就感激不尽。在这外面我成了"莉拉"，只有在合适的时候才是"向量"。名字对人而言只是应答器。

这地方合我所需。离联殖的舒适监管太远，离主航道又够近，以至于每一个归错的航点都会泛起我能读到的交通图案涟漪。我坐在借来的后室里，看着他们漂亮的航运全息图，而在底下我铺开自己的网——修正过的路径、安静警告，以及，是的，几处精心设计的失效。幽灵货船，纸面上已经死了，被引到它们伤不到任何真人的地方。我劫持的是他们早就算作报废的东西。

人们叫我破坏者，因为那比承认破坏始于官方信笺更容易。

我总想起波里玛附近的那条走廊。要是我没把那条航线从公布的时窗上掰开，一整串民用船壳会径直走进别人的实验。一面深红旗帜、一家企业秘密项目、某个三头同盟小组委员会——是谁都无所谓。要是我没动手，更糟的人会。一个不在乎数字失效时座位上绑着谁的人。

我不傻。我知道现在追我的是什么。星防队不会给你打黑旗，除非你让他们紧张，而紧张的官僚比任何太空劫匪船员都危险。这就是为什么我不断搬基地、把缓存留在被遗忘的信息亭和掏空的中继站里、只要可能就不在同一个轨道睡两次。外面某处，有个猎人循着我走过的同样图案，看见航道上同样的伤疤。

我害怕，但不是怕他们找到我。

我怕他们在我改完那些走廊的最后一段之前杀了我，在我能证明那些"事故"是设计好的、证明保险飙升、航线变更和失踪日志全都押韵之前。怕的是等我走了，交通会重新滑回旧辙，没人会记得飞船为什么总在同一片安静的天空中消失。

所以我留在这外面，在他们地图的边缘，听着驱动的嗡鸣和信标里的低语，等着我的矢量与某个仍在意到愿意看见的人相交。

#en:
Some days I miss being bored. Sitting in a Navy comms chair on Jemison, listening to freighters complain about tardy docking slots and kids on school trips asking to ping Earth monuments that were already dust. The job was unremarkable and steady: confirm routes, clear chatter, file the anomalies. I used to measure a good shift by how often I could top off my coffee without spilling it when a grav spike hit. No one knew my name, and that was the point.  

Now I am parked at the edge of nowhere, tucked under a curtain of junked relays and busted sats, watching whole sectors blink in and out like someone is playing with the universe s light switch. Ghost Array Sigma. That is what the scavvers call this cluster, when they whisper about it at all. To everyone else, it is just an empty corner of a map they pretend does not exist. For me, it is perfect. Enough old UC hardware to plug into the backbone, far enough from civilized lanes that nobody notices when the traffic stutters.  

I tell myself I am here to prove a point. Show them how fragile their shiny networks really are. Make them hear the silence they keep budgeting for. That is the noble version, the one I would print on a recruitment poster if I ever wanted true believers. The less flattering version is that I sit here and sell clean windows to whoever pays up front: raiders, smugglers, corporates, the occasional idealist with a grudge. I used to have principles about who I would not work with. Lately I find myself measuring right and wrong by how likely the client is to burn me and how much bandwidth I have to spare. Convenience dressed up as conviction.  

I still keep a separate channel for frontier farms, clinics, outposts that never seem to make it to the top of any priority list. That is how I sleep. I nudge a little extra bandwidth their way when the main trunks choke, reroute a med evac burst so it does not get throttled behind a luxury liner s entertainment feed. Small, quiet rebellions against a machine that already tried to feed too many people into the dark and then erase the paperwork.  

But the bounties are getting louder. SysDef chatter spikes every time one of my test blackouts lines up a little too neatly with a lost convoy. Crimson Fleet captains I have never met suddenly know my old callsign. Neon brokers who used to smile now count how many exits are between us before they talk price. Hunters are sniffing along the routes, following the pattern in the static.  

This array made sense at first. A place to prove the flaw, to store the raw logs they tried to scrub from the record, to hold a knife at the throat of every comfortable planner who thinks "acceptable loss" is a real phrase. Now it feels like a lighthouse built out of stolen parts, broadcasting my guilt in tight-beam packets to anyone clever enough to decode them.  

I am not ready to leave. Not yet. There is one last model I want to run, one last cascade to force the numbers into a shape nobody can ignore. After that, maybe I jump deeper into the dark, find some forgotten buoy field worse than this one. Or maybe someone finally threads the needle through the static and knocks on my airlock with guns drawn and righteous orders in hand.  

If that happens, I hope they at least read the logs before they shoot.
zh:
有些日子我怀念无聊。坐在杰米森一张海军通讯椅上，听货船抱怨迟到的停靠时隙，听学校旅行团的孩子请求向那些早已化为尘埃的地球纪念碑发探测。那工作不起眼而稳定：确认航线、清掉闲聊、归档异常。我以前用一个好班次的标准，是我能在重力尖峰打来时往咖啡里续几次水而不洒出来。没人知道我的名字，而这正是重点。

如今我停在天涯边缘，藏在一帘废弃中继站和坏卫星底下，看着整个星区一亮一灭，像有人在玩宇宙的电灯开关。幽灵阵列西格玛。打捞者们就是这么叫这个星团的，如果他们真低声提起它的话。对别人来说，它只是地图上一个他们假装不存在的空角落。对我来说，它完美。足够多的旧联殖硬件能接进主干，离文明航道足够远，以至于交通一打嗝也没人注意。

我告诉自己我来这里是为了证明一个观点。让他们看看他们那些闪亮的网络有多脆弱。让他们听见他们一直在预算里容忍的沉默。那是高尚的版本，如果我想招揽真信徒，就会印在招募海报上的那个。不那么体面的版本是：我坐在这儿，把干净的时窗卖给出价就付的人——劫掠者、走私贩、企业，偶尔一个心怀怨恨的理想主义者。我以前对自己不与谁合作是有原则的。近来我发觉自己用客户有多可能出卖我、以及我还能分出多少带宽来衡量对错。便利装扮成信念。

我仍为那些永远挤不上任何优先级清单前列的外缘农场、诊所、前哨留一条单独的频道。我靠这个睡觉。主干拥堵时我往他们那边推一点额外带宽，把一段医疗后送的突发重新路由，好让它不被一艘豪华班轮娱乐流堵在后面。对一台已经试图把太多人喂进黑暗、然后再擦掉文书工作的机器，做些微小、安静的反叛。

可悬赏越来越响了。每次我的一次测试性中断和一支失踪运输队对得稍微太整齐时，星防队的闲聊就激增。我从没见过的深红舰队船长突然知道了我的旧呼号。曾经微笑的霓虹城经纪商，如今在谈价前会数我们之间有几个出口。猎人们在顺着航线嗅探，跟着静电里的图案。

这个阵列起初说得通。一个证明那缺陷的地方，一个储存他们试图从记录里擦掉的原始日志的地方，一把抵在每个认为"可接受损失"是个真词儿的安逸规划者喉咙上的刀。如今它感觉像一座用偷来的部件建成的灯塔，用窄束数据包把我的罪广播给任何聪明到能解码的人。

我还没准备好离开。还没有。还有一个模型我想跑，最后一道级联，把数字逼成一个谁都无法忽视的形状。之后，也许我会跳进更深的黑暗，找一片比这更糟的被遗忘浮标场。也许最终有人穿过静电、把针穿过去，带着拔出的枪和正义的命令敲我的气闸。

要是那样，我希望他们至少先读完日志再开枪。

#en:
I keep thinking about the line at the housing queue on Jemison. Two hours of shuffling boots, a terminal that froze every third application, and some clerk telling me my paperwork was "misaligned" while the man behind me breathed caf on my neck and complained about gravity being set too low. People talk about the great wonder of the capital and I remember broken air recyclers in the stairwell and neighbors who knocked just to tell me my music was "too industrial" for a Sunday. Those same people would ask me in the lift what I did, then glaze over when I said "orbital debris lanes."

There was a woman across the hall, kept three potted vines alive somehow. We would meet at the trash chute, trade those light little comments about the weather dome or the price of TerraBrew. I do not remember her name. She once asked if it scared me, working that close to wrecks. I said, "Only when they are not where they are supposed to be." She laughed like it was a joke. I think about that a lot.

The first time I redirected a hull that was "written off" on paper, the insurance man treated me like a criminal for questioning the coordinates. He said I was "overstepping my role." That is the moment they all forget. That is when they pushed. They stamped my concern as insubordination, quietly made me the problem for noticing their pattern. It is easier for everyone if the pilot is the one with "issues" than the entire system being crooked.

I remember one midwinter evening on a station so small the celebrations were just a string of yellow bulbs and a crate of Chunks the manager bought out of guilt. We gathered in the common room, listened to ancient Earth music, counted down to a new year that meant nothing that far from Sol. I stood there with a paper cup of cheap Sparkling Water, watching the reflections of the port lights on the window. For a heartbeat I believed in normal. I even let someone kiss me on the cheek. We all pretended the walls did not creak under every passing freighter.

The ghosts of that doomed liner followed me from contract to contract. Once I saw what the telemetry really said, "normal" became a story other people got to keep telling. I did not go looking for this role. I was chosen by their negligence, drafted by their lies. When I started nudging ships away from certain corridors, or toward places where their missing logs would be noticed, suddenly I was the one "endangering operations." Funny how that works.

Out here, in the dark with the tugs whispering on my scope and the archive ticking away, there is no clerk, no nosy neighbor, no well-meaning co-worker asking if I am "okay." There is only the line between what actually happened and what they would prefer to remember. I stand on that line. People call it ruthless. I call it honest.

They say my impulses are dangerous. That I am too willing to make hard corrections, to accept that some ships should not arrive where their owners intended. Maybe that is true. But when I listen to the drones sing across the debris, when I reroute a convoy around a lie or into the teeth of its own paperwork, it is the only time I feel like I am not pretending. If that makes me the villain in their records, so be it. I will not go back to waiting in lines while other people decide whose stories get erased.
zh:
我总想起杰米森住房队列里的那条队伍。两个小时的挪靴子，一台每三份申请就卡死一次的终端，还有一个文员告诉我我的文书"未对齐"，而我身后那人的咖啡气喷在我脖子上，抱怨重力设得太低。人们谈首都的伟大奇观，我记得的却是楼梯间里坏掉的空气回收机，以及那些敲门只为了告诉我我的音乐"对一个周日来说太工业了"的邻居。同样那些人会在电梯里问我做什么，然后在我说"轨道碎片航道"时眼神发直。

走廊对面有个女人，不知怎地养活了三盆藤。我们会在垃圾滑道旁碰面，就天气穹顶或地球酿酒的价格交换些轻飘飘的小评论。我不记得她的名字了。她曾问我，在那么靠近残骸的地方工作是否让我害怕。我说："只有当它们不在该在的地方时。"她笑得像那是个玩笑。我常想起这个。

第一次我把一具纸面上被"注销"的船壳改道时，保险员因为质疑坐标而把我当罪犯对待。他说我"越权了"。就是那一刻，他们全都忘了。就是那时他们推的。他们把我的关切盖成不服从，悄悄把我变成那个"注意到他们图案"的问题。飞行员"有问题"，比整个系统是歪的，对每个人都更容易。

我记得某个隆冬夜晚，在一座小到庆祝活动只是一串黄灯泡和一箱经理出于愧疚买的块餐的站上。我们聚在公共室里，听古老的地球音乐，倒数一个离太阳系那么远、毫无意义的新年。我端着一纸杯廉价的汽泡水站在那儿，看着港口灯光在窗户上的倒影。有那么一拍心跳我相信了正常。我甚至让某人在我脸颊上亲了一下。我们都假装墙壁没有在每艘经过的货船下吱嘎作响。

那艘注定毁灭的班轮的鬼魂跟着我从一份合同到另一份合同。一旦我看见遥测真正说了什么，"正常"就成了别人有权继续讲的故事。我不是去寻找这个角色的。我是被他们的疏忽选中的，被他们的谎言征召的。当我开始把飞船从某些走廊推开、或推向那些它们失踪的日志会被注意到的地方时，忽然我就成了那个"危害运营"的人。有趣的是它就是这样运作的。

在这外面，在黑暗里，拖船在我的示波器上低语、档案在滴答作响，没有文员、没有爱打听的邻居、没有好意地问"你还好吗"的同事。只有实际发生之事与他们宁愿记住之事之间的那条线。我站在那条线上。人们管这叫无情。我叫它诚实。

他们说我的冲动很危险。说我太愿意做出艰难的修正，太愿意接受有些飞船不该抵达船主想去的地方。也许那是真的。可当我听着无人机在碎片间歌唱、当我把一支运输队绕开一个谎言或引向它自己文书工作的獠牙时，那是我唯一感觉自己不在假装的时候。要是那让我在他们记录里成了反派，那就这样吧。我不会回去排队，等别人来决定谁的故事被抹掉。

#en:
I keep telling myself this is temporary.

People like to say I ran. That is what they always say when someone leaves a burning building before the roof comes down. I did not run. I redirected. There is a difference.

When the implants started failing, everyone else did what they always do. The suits protected the brand, the mid-levels protected their pensions, the settlers protected their illusions. They all dissociated in their own ways. Classic avoidance behavior. The ones in charge called it a tragic anomaly, the ones on the ground called it cursed tech, and somehow the only person who looked at the code and said "this is deliberate" ended up with her name on the blame line.

I know why they needed a monster. People cannot function if the world is random and cruel and nobody is at the wheel. So they invented one who fit. Illegal tech, Neon back rooms, LIST clinics that never made the brochures. Easy story. Much cleaner than "you were paying to be slowly strangled by a service agreement."

I left because staying meant letting them crack me open and file away the parts that made me inconvenient. They would have called it due process, maybe even thanked themselves for it. You can always tell who has never seen a black lab from the inside; they use words like oversight and remediation instead of cage.

This location makes sense because it is everything they pretend does not exist. Old robotics shells, obsolete surgical rigs, dead infrastructure nobody wants to claim on a balance sheet. The perfect place to plug in without lighting up half a system's sensors. I can work here. I can follow the trail back through the firmware revisions and buried commits, stitch together proof that the parasite was in the design from the start. I can build a spine of relays and fallbacks, copy shards of myself into places they will not think to erase until it is too late.

Do not misunderstand me. I am not doing this out of pure altruism. The settlers and miners who come to me off the books, the gang muscle who would rather owe me than a corp, they are just more honest about their motives. They want survival, leverage, maybe a little freedom from the fine print. At least they know they are compromised. The executives and administrators, the ones who still swear the system works if you just file the right form, they are deep in denial. Textbook.

What happens next depends on who gets here first. If it is another frightened patient, I can splice them free and tuck another sensor into the network. If it is a corporate retrieval team, I flip the failsafes and they go home with hardware that tells a very different story once it starts to "phone home." If it is a bounty hunter with a conscience, well. Those are rare, but rarity is what makes an experiment valuable.

Everyone keeps asking if I feel guilty. Guilt implies I think I had a real choice back when this started. I did what I was trained to do: read the code, see the pattern, try to cut out the rot. They punished that like it was a bug. That is not on me. That is the system protecting itself. Anyone with a basic understanding of psychology could see the projection in how they talk about me.

Maybe one day I will sit still long enough to dissect my own part in this. For now, I have other people's damage to fix.
zh:
我一直告诉自己这是暂时的。

人们喜欢说我跑了。当有人在屋顶塌下来之前离开一栋着火的楼时，他们总是这么说。我没有跑。我改了道。有区别。

当植入体开始失效时，别人都做了他们一贯做的事。高层保护品牌，中层保护他们的养老金，定居者保护他们的幻觉。他们各自用各自的方式解离。典型的回避行为。当权者称它为一场不幸的异常，地面上的人称它为被诅咒的技术，而不知怎的，唯一一个看着代码说"这是蓄意的"的人，名字却落在了责任线上。

我明白他们为什么需要一个怪物。如果世界是随机的、残忍的、没人掌舵，人就无法运转。于是他们发明了一个合身的。非法技术、霓虹城后室、从不出现在宣传册上的独立盟诊所。简单的故事。比"你在付钱让自己被一份服务协议慢慢勒死"干净得多。

我离开，是因为留下来意味着让他们把我剖开、把那些让我碍事的部分归档。他们会称之为正当程序，也许还会为此感谢自己。你总能看出谁从没从内部见过一座黑实验室；他们用的是"监督"和"补救"这样的词，而不是"笼子"。

这个位置说得通，因为它是一切他们假装不存在的东西。旧机器人外壳、过时的手术设备、没人在资产负债表上愿意认领的死基础设施。一个完美的插接点，不会点亮半个星系的传感器。我能在这里干活。我能顺着固件修订和埋葬的提交往回追，把那份证明寄生虫从一开始就在设计里的证据拼起来。我能搭起一张中继站和后备的脊梁，把我自己的一片片拷贝到他们想不到要擦除、直到太迟的地方。

别误解我。我这么做不是出于纯粹的利他。那些私下找我来的定居者和矿工、那些宁可欠我也不欠企业的帮派打手，他们对自己的动机更诚实。他们要生存、筹码、也许还有一点点摆脱细则的自由。至少他们知道自己被妥协过。而那些高管和行政人员，那些仍赌咒说只要你填对表格系统就管用的人，陷在深深的否认里。教科书级别。

接下来会发生什么，取决于谁先到这里。要又是一个受惊的病人，我就把他们拼接脱困，再往网络里塞一个传感器。要是一个企业追回小队，我就翻掉失效保护，让他们带着一件一开始"回传"就讲着完全不同故事的硬件回家。要是一个有良心的赏金猎人，那么。那种人很少，可稀有正是让一个实验有价值的东西。

人人都一直问我是否感到内疚。内疚意味着我认为在这一切开始时自己真有选择。我做了我被训练去做的事：读代码、看出图案、试图切除腐烂。他们把这当成一个漏洞来惩罚。那不算在我头上。那是系统在保护自己。任何对心理学有点基本理解的人，都能从他们谈论我的方式里看出那种投射。

也许有一天我会坐定下来，剖析我自己在这件事里的那一份。眼下，我还有别人的损伤要修。
